segments.txt: First of all, I must express my gratitude to Alla SWT. For allowing all of us, myself included, to breathe and reach this Friday once again.
And something I always emphasize to myself is that this Friday could be our very last one. There is no guarantee that we will see another Friday again.

Which means, what I am trying to say is, I want all of us, myself included, to remain mindful and fearful of Alla SWT. In reality, we don't necessarily have to think that we won't see another Friday, but we
should think that every single day could be our last before Kiyama arrives. This means do not let living in this dunya be our final destination.

But let this dunya be like. A passing path. I often make a simple comparison that if our goal is the Akira, or entering his Paradise, then this worldly life is like a gas station when we go on a trip, right?
You all have probably had the chance to go on a holiday or travel out of town to go somewhere beautiful. We have to stop at gas stations all the time, don't we?
And naturally, those gas stations have many amenities. There's a 7-Eleven, there's a coffee shop, there's fuel, there's food, there are restrooms,
or nowadays, some even have camping grounds right at the gas station. But what would you say to someone who says, once they stop at the station, I'm not going
to the beach or cow-yay anymore, I'll just stay here at the station. Why is that? Well, everything is already here for us. Why would we need to go to the beach anymore?
You would probably laugh at that friend and ask, have you lost your mind? The gas station is just a temporary place to stop, but our real goal is at the final destination.
It lies at that beautiful sea. So, don't let the temptations at the gas station, which is just a rest stop, trick you into thinking it's the final destination.
This is the same, it's like a person who is lost in this worldly life. When looking at everything we have, food, clothing, shelter, a good spouse, children, or even

the status and titles we achieve, don't let it become your end goal, a believer must see it only as a passage. But viewing the world as a passage isn't just about empty words or trying to sound profound.
To put it simply, it's not enough to just say, this world is a passage, and we must head to the afterlife. It measures how much you truly understand this is your daily actions.
It means nothing to say the world is a passage and the afterlife is the goal. If, in the days we spend, our hearts are actually consumed by other things.
If you break it down into 100%, my brothers and sisters, everyone needs to look at themselves. We cannot judge this because the heart is something we cannot know.
We cannot read anyone, only Allah, SWT, knows our hearts best. Try to examine your heart, in one day, if we assume your thoughts are 100%. What percentage of your heart is focused on the afterlife?
What percentage of your heart is filled with worldly worries? And if, when compared, the percentage for the afterlife is lower, that means saying, the world
is a passage and the afterlife is the goal, is just empty talk. Therefore, brothers and sisters, try to check the balance of your heart, what you give to

the world versus what you give to the afterlife, and see which one outweighs the other. And please, do not misinterpret my words. It does not mean that Islam requires us to renounce the world, nor does it mean we should
become ascetics who stop working, focus only on religion, and abandon everything. We certainly are not told to do that because otherwise, Allah would not have revealed Sharia

laws concerning other matters, right? Whether it concerns the social sector or matters of social assistance, regarding the pursuit of a career, halal and haram, and our food and belongings, Allah knows well that we must

live in this world. But we must live in this world by viewing it as a tool, as a passage, not as the ultimate goal. And in Islam, we view everything that is other than the deen, other than the religion of Allah,

as a tool, my brothers and sisters. Such as what, like a mobile phone, for example, we use it as a tool to achieve our goal in the hereafter, like what, for instance, like the mobile phone being used to live stream
right now. We are using it as a tool to reach the goal of doing good deeds and seeking rewards, right? Or an airplane. We use an airplane to perform umrah or hajj.
We use it as a tool. But it is not the goal, nor should we be obsessed with it as our primary objective, and the same applies to other matters.
Matters like politics, for example. We must view them as tools to be used to fulfill the sharia of Allah. Which will bring us closer to Allah, and the meaning of being close to Allah, is that which
keeps us away from sins, away from shirk, away from bitter, away from various acts of disobedience. Only then can we call it a tool used to serve the goal.
But if we claim we are using it as a tool, yet what is the final destination, if the result that comes out is committing sins, if the result that comes out is committing shirk, if
the result that comes out is committing acts of disobedience, even if you say, I am using it as a tool, using this thing as a tool, but the final outcome is that, we don't call

it a tool, that means you are using it as the final goal. Therefore, in Islam, we view this worldly life as a tool to attain the hereafter. Everything must be based on this foundation, regardless of the various professions, sending

children to study secular subjects is fine, that's okay, but studying religion is good, and secular studies are fine too. But ultimately, does any study bring our children or ourselves closer to Allah?
It's not about looking at it like, okay, I sent my child to become a doctor, being a doctor is good, I'm not saying it isn't, and Muslim society needs it.
But if you pride yourself only on your child becoming a doctor, yet when you check their faith in their heart, they doubt the existence of Allah, I don't call that success.
I don't call that successfully raising a child. As successfully raising a child means no matter how great or humble they become, their heart is with Allah, religion comes first.
Therefore, I do not consider it a cause for celebration to see our Muslim intellectuals, those who finish degrees abroad in secular fields or sciences, some whom I've met, where Muslim
society cheers, oh, they're the representatives of the intellectual class, they've finished in science, when abroad, became doctors, and so on.

But when you look at their faith, some deny God, some contradict religious principles, are they doubt them? For instance, having studied much science, they use scientific theories to question religion.
They study science, then come across the claim that Prophet Adam was created from clay. Well, how could he be created from clay when the theory of evolution explains things, and

it doesn't mention the first human, and where did the dinosaurs go? Dinosaurs aren't in the Quran, for example. Or, having studied science, they say the earth is billions of years old, and the universe

is tens of billions of years old. Then, looking at the Quran, he says he created this world, right, in a period of, six days. Six days or six periods of time, then they start interpreting, six days, what does that mean?
How could it possibly be six days, you see where this starts? This is a sign that I don't call success. This is just a reminder for us all to start with.
Now I will present the single piece of evidence that is sufficient for both scientists and laypeople like us to recognize the existence of Allah without any doubt or skepticism.
I only need to present this one piece of evidence, and it is enough. And modern science actually supports what I'm about to say next. But this is not me trying to twist the Quran to fit science.
I must state first that distorting the Quran to fit any ideology is considered wrong. However, if there are certain facts in nature that we study and they happen to align with the
Quran, then that is not a problem. I want to establish this principle first, the Quran is a book of signs. It is a book that explains how we can be saved from the hellfire.
It is not a science textbook, I must clarify that first. The Quran is not a science textbook. This means the Quran does not necessarily discuss every single scientific matter in detail,
that is not its purpose. Therefore, when it comes to certain scientific facts, what kind of facts, for instance? For example, the existence of night and day, which can be verified as true.

The fact that the earth rotates on its axis. The fact that it orbits. These are facts that the Quran has already mentioned. As Allah has shown us the signs of the night, the day, the sun, and the moon, right?
So, these facts, not just speculative theories, that align with the Quran allow us to confirm that the one who stated these truths in the Quran long before we discovered the details,

how did he know these truths? How could Muhammad, peace be upon him, know the truths of the world and the universe, being an Arab man who could not read or write, was not a philosopher, and was not a scientist, yet
he revealed these truths 1400 years ago? This is the main point. The evidence I will present today is a single point, and it is sufficient for those with

a pure heart. What is the scientific discovery that tells us that the universe we live in, my brothers and sisters, had a beginning? Ah, if we talk about modern times, you might ask, what is so surprising about the universe
having a beginning, because, certainly, nothing has existed eternally alongside Allah. Only Allah exists eternally and is independent of all things.

Therefore, everything that has been created must have had a beginning. Indeed, in our Aqeeda, faith, this is not surprising. But would you believe that in non-Muslim societies, this answer only became clear less than 100
years ago, or perhaps not even more than 200 years ago? What does that mean? People in previous eras, my brothers and sisters, we are now in the year 2026, the year 2026
AD. In the period before 1920, the period before that, brothers and sisters. If it or not, there was a major ambiguity for people back then, as those who rejected
God claimed that the universe had existed from the very beginning. The universe had existed eternally, but why would they say that? You might ask, why would they have to say that?
The answer is that by trying to make the universe have no beginning and exist eternally, they could argue that the universe did not need a creator.
Because in their philosophy, it might be true that if this universe existed from the start, it is like a God, replacing God. God has existed all along with no beginning and no end.
It means the universe does not need an explanation for how it came to be if it has existed eternally. At that time, those who rejected God tried to anchor this explanation in science.
Specifically, someone like Albert Einstein sought to confirm this theory, well, not a fact, but to confirm this theory, that the universe is eternal.
But later on, new discoveries by a scientist named Edwin Hubble and many other scientists revealed that there is actually evidence that the universe has a beginning.
Do you know how he observed this, my friends? Edwin Hubble was very clever. He looked at the stars at night, my friends, when we look up, they shine light towards us,
right? So, Edwin Hubble captured the light waves from those stars. Those are actually galaxies, they are galaxies that send light to us, which we see as tiny
dots. Actually, when we zoom in to look, my friends, it's not just a single star like that. It's like, when you zoom in, there are millions upon millions of stars in there, a distant cluster
of stars. Anyway, scientists captured that light to see where these stars were shining from. Did it travel far? We wanted to know how many kilometers away they were.
They captured it, and it turned out that what they discovered was more than just the distance of the stars. They discovered that the light was running away from us.
In simple terms, the stars we see are not standing still, my friends. They are moving away, fleeing from us, fleeing from our Earth in every direction, where they
are running to, no one knows. Scientists are still puzzled by this today. We don't know where they are heading, but what Edwin Hubble concluded was this.
If today the stars seem to be fleeing from us in every direction, right? Then what if we travel back in time? That means before that, the stars must have been closer to us.
It means if we wind time back to the beginning, all the stars must have been clustered together in one place, and then at a certain point, they gradually expand it outward.
This leads to the conclusion that the universe is not a static universe, but one that is constantly expanding. And its expansion confirms its beginning that one day they were all once stuck together.
Believe it or not, all a SWT, declared that the universe is constantly expanding even before Edwin Hubble discovered this fact. As he said, W.A.

is the one who is constantly expanding it. You can look up the word in the Arabic language. It is a word that indicates an ongoing action. This means that all estated long ago that he has been spreading and expanding the universe
all along, and the fact that Edwin Hubble and many scientists say the universe was once joined together and then expanded from the beginning.

Which we call the Big Bang Theory. The Quran described it even more accurately. It is in Surah Al-Ambia, the 21st verse, 30. Yes, where Allah calls upon the disbelievers to look at this as proof of God's existence.
As he stated, do the disbelievers not see that the heavens and the earth were once joined together? And he is the one who separated them both.
And he created every living thing using water as the fundamental element in their creation. Even science has only just confirmed these things.
How is it possible that Muhammad could state such a profound truth? I cannot imagine, brothers and sisters, I truly cannot imagine how a man in Arabia, in
the desert, in a system without scientific organizations, unable to read or write, I cannot fathom how prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, could have come up with this.
And even if we were to assume that Muhammad just made it all up himself. And why is it that this fabrication happens to be correct in every dimension regarding
the universe, life, and other matters I haven't even touched upon today? Why would Muhammad guess everything and be right about it all? I'm posing this question to the disbelievers.

But of course, Muslims have clearly answered that this is something Muhammad, as a human, could not have known on his own. Unless God, Allah, the Lord of the worlds, revealed this knowledge to the prophet Muhammad, peace
be upon him. For what purpose, for what purpose? To serve as a testament and evidence that prophet Muhammad is truly a Rasul, or a messenger,

sent by God. So, what does this mean? It means that if prophet Muhammad is truly from God and the Quran is truly from God, then all of humanity must follow him, humanity must follow this man to be saved from the hellfire.

It is no longer about following other scriptures. One must follow this man, you must lower your ego to see if you can follow him. Especially when it has been proven today that he is the messenger of Allah.
So, coming back to the conclusion of why we must fear Allah, this is my answer to the disbelievers. It means that since Allah is the creator of this universe, and he has declared his ownership
and stated that he knows its details far better than humans do, it means that we, who are in his home, in his universe, must be mindful of ourselves.
Do not be arrogant, acting as if you know more about everything than God, while possessing scientific knowledge that is not even 1% of his knowledge.
Yet, you dare to use that knowledge to reject or doubt Allah, to doubt the creator. You study a bit of medicine, learn a little about the body, and become so arrogant that you

claim there is no creator and think you know everything. This is extreme arrogance for those who lack humility. Especially for Muslims who study science but fail to know how to humble themselves before
Allah. Do not think that your knowledge makes you all knowing. This proven, even Einstein, whom people praise as brilliant, was once refuted.
Those who claim the universe had no beginning were eventually proven wrong by Hubble. What does this mean? Science is just like that. Don't dare use it to deny the creator.

Realize that as humans living in the universe he created, we must acknowledge we are in his home and must follow his rules. When we visit someone's house, brothers and sisters, don't you agree we must follow the

host? You can't just open their fridge and eat whatever you want, or sleep in anyone's room without permission, can you? If we humans get angry at that, then how can you think you can live in the creator's universe
doing whatever you please? That is illogical, so today, now that you know the universe has a creator, we are living in a home he built for us.

Be mindful of yourself. Because if you are not, and remain arrogant, you must prepare for the day of judgment in the afterlife. For he has already stated that for the disbelievers, their end is the hellfire, and for the patient
believers, their end is paradise. May we all be granted entry into the highest paradise, Ferdaus, by Allah Subhanahu W. Adala. Amin.

segments.txt: This is my favorite chapter, look at the way he tells the story. I feel like it has such charm. The chapter title is, in just 50 years, no one will know us anymore.

And they might not even know we ever existed in this world. I think the way this chapter sets up the story telling is incredibly good. He opens the story well, he starts by telling us he's at a certain place.
His phrasing uses the words. At the end of the path, flanked by overgrown grass on both sides, an old, dilapidated house appeared before me.
I called out the owner's name familiarly at the old wooden door, but there was no answer. As soon as he describes it, it creates a shot in my mind.
He describes it so vividly that I can see it clearly. Then he says, it had been quite a long time since I last visited this house. Calling it an abandoned house now wouldn't be wrong.
So, I took the liberty of slowly nudging the door open to see if anyone was inside. Just in the musty smell of the house filled my eyes and nostrils.
To my right, there was an old wooden staircase leading up to a level that wasn't exactly a second floor. It was just a raised platform partitioned into a bedroom.
I walked up the stairs cautiously all the way. The wooden floor was in such bad shape, ready to break at any moment. It's hard to believe it had deteriorated this much.

On the left side was a room piled high with stacks of clothes. I scanned the room once more to make sure no one was inside. Suddenly, memories of the past, which I tried to piece together with the present like scattered
puzzle pieces, flooded my mind in the silence of this house. When he narrates it like this, it makes you picture yourself walking into an old abandoned

house, with a room on the right. With piles of clothes on the left, and then you start thinking about what this place used to be. It shows he's implying that he must have been here before when it wasn't like this.
Yeah, and the thing is, it makes us wonder, where is this place? Where did he go? It makes us curious. Then he said that in the meantime, he heard a sound.
It was the voice of someone talking in their sleep. And it was just as he thought. There was someone in the house. He was curled up inside this cluttered room.
He didn't take long for me to realize it was the Quran being recited in a rambling way. It was a verse from one of the suras in the 30th Jews.
It was being uttered from the depths of the memories of someone sleeping and dreaming. This man curled up there. Just imagine, mumbling prayers in an abandoned house.
I wasn't sure if it was a symptom of drug addiction, because his condition showed a very emaciated body. And it was known that he was a victim of drug abuse.
He worked odd jobs with unstable income for quite a long time, and his condition now looked so different. He saw this person curled up in a drug-addicted state, an odd job worker with unstable income
living in an abandoned house. And he spoke to highlight the difference, saying that his condition now looked so different from the first day I knew him, like he was a completely different person.
It shows he wasn't like this before. He creates questions because he didn't just give the answer right away. He has what you call flair, flair in storytelling.
Finally, he said that years ago, this guy was one of the handsome young men. His family had good status. He was hardworking. He was the crush of all the girls in the village.
But they were disappointed when they found out he had married a woman who was just as good looking. Oh, his life seemed so good in the past.
Why does it make us ask the question, yeah, but why is he sleeping like that nowadays? Yes, good looking, good status, married to a good looking woman.
Yes, it was totally perfect when they found out he had married a woman who was just as good looking. Both of them decided to work in the capital city, hoping to build a life together.
But not long after that, his wife was in a car accident. A car hit her, leaving her seriously injured. She had to undergo emergency brain surgery.
It turns out this man not only had to give extra care to his wife. He also had a little daughter, another cute one that he had to look after.
After this event, his life changed and was never the same again, because from having a good job before. He resigned to take care of his disabled, sick wife, and his child.
And with the circumstances he faced, there was sadness in his life. There was a point where he got caught up in the cycle of drug addiction, which finally became
the start of a major change for his family. It was a complete turnaround from when his parents were considered middle class and well respected.
But unfortunately, both sons and this family were addicted to drugs. I don't know why the first one got addicted, but the second one is the person currently sleeping

in this house. I once came to this house 30 years ago. This house looked beautiful, full of life, clean, tidy, and very livable. The people in the house seemed wealthier than many families in the neighborhood.
But to put it simply, after his parents passed away, the two sons got hooked on drugs. The house fell apart, left with nothing, becoming the state you see here.
He told it as a story. He walked to that room and saw the photo albums scattered around. He looked into the photo album and went through each picture one by one.
He reflected on how, in the past, in those pictures, they were once happy. Everyone, and now we don't even know where the people in the photos are.

Some have already passed away. It made him reflect that the photo album and the actual atmosphere of the house are very different. The inside that everyone in life must have gone through something like this.

That the moments where we were happy and spent time together. In the end, when the event passes, it's as if it never happened at all. The events in those pictures, those beautiful images, are like a fairy tale that once happened
and now we don't know where it went. In the end, everyone's final destination is to fade away and die, leaving only memories of what once existed on this earth, and there is nothing else.

He offered a very profound lesson here. It makes us finally have to reflect on ourselves that, in the end, we all must die in part ways. Each person accumulates so many stories in their life, yet in the end, they must die anyway.
He leaves this thought at the end of the chapter. I'm skipping this part. If you want to read more, go buy it and see, for those who like this style of storytelling.
As I said before, it's not exactly academic language, it's more of a literary style. It's enjoyable to read, and the good thing is that literature written by Salafi's is rare.
You can read it alongside religious books. As we want something relaxing, but relaxing in the right way, I think this one is good. He ends this chapter with a point I really like.
He concludes by saying that every human on this earth has memories of millions of good and bad life events. But sadly, when the time comes, they will fade away with time.
They will disappear into time as if nothing ever happened. And this time will consume everything until everything is obliterated. Only the Creator remains, the one who still exists.
Our life is so short, and none of us on this earth know what will happen to us today or tomorrow. But what we can do is, when good things happen, be very grateful.

And if bad things happen to us, be patient and remember the one who owns all things. Because in the end, we all must return to him. He then cited Surah Al-Bakara, verse 156, which means, those who, when a disaster strikes
them, say, indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to him we will return. This was the conclusion of the chapter, which I was very impressed by.

I have to say that I like it for two reasons. First, I like the style of how the story opens and unfolds. It has many plot twists, and second, I like its implication in the meaning it conveys, because
it's something I've always thought about too. That in the end, we all have to disappear, everyone who vanishes from this world. And in the end, we used to think our death mattered so much.
People who think about suicide often feel that if I die, everyone will pay more attention to me. But you'll have to be sad if you see me dead.

Really? To those I love who turned their backs on me, you're definitely going to regret it. It's like a cry. A cry for attention. We think we are so important to the world, but in the end, the day we actually die, it's
only a few days before they go back to their lives. At most, they might just leave a comment expressing their sorrow for us. And after a day or two, they just go on living their lives.
They go have wives, husbands, children, and stressful jobs. And one day, we become just a memory that they might occasionally think back on, like,
yeah, back then, that person used to be around, they used to do this. Yeah, that's it. Yes, we just become a fleeting thought in people's minds.
A mere fragment of attention. A fragment, because in the end, everyone is so caught up in their own stuff. It's really just that. No matter how much they love you, it's just that.
So we just know that we have to be caught up in our own lives instead. Because eventually, we're going to die like everyone else anyway. Whatever happens to our families, life goes on.
In the end, people don't keep us in their hearts all that much. Therefore, this serves as a cautionary tale.
